On `main` it already took 11 min 55 s. The full analysis is in section 7 of [the case study](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-45-bac51f6e4d8d/docs/case-studies/issue-45/README.md).\\n\\n- **Root cause.** Every framed element declared 49 custom properties of its own (`calc()` of `var()`, a 36-point polygon, and the sizes and positions of 20 layers). WebKit compares every inherited custom property of every element when `<html>` restyles, which the issue #27 audit does on each slider key press.\\n- **Fix.** The root computes the lengths of each scale once as typed `@property` lengths. Framed elements draw from them in properties that do not inherit (`src/skins.frames.properties.css`).\\n- **Measured.** `experiments/issue-45-webkit-diagnose.mjs` ran as a temporary CI step. One restyle of `/settings/` in WebKit dropped from 1680 ms to 378 ms. For comparison, the same Matrix look on `main` takes 272 ms and the Glass look on `main` 107 ms.\\n- **Tried and dropped.** Each of these was timed with `experiments/issue-45-ab-sheets.mjs`, which alternates sheet sets A, B, A, B so machine load slows both alike. None helped beyond the noise:\\n  - unitless numbers per element instead of root lengths (390 ms against 340 ms);\\n  - dropping `--fx-scale` (269 against 298 ms);\\n  - `content-visibility: auto` on the off-screen settings groups (WebKit still restyles them).\\n\\n  `experiments/issue-45-inherited-count-micro.mjs` shows the floor that is left: 500 inherited root lengths cost about 26 ms on 1800 elements.\\n- **Time limits.** The job still does not fit in 15 minutes. The page has 111 sliders instead of 93, the default look restyles about 2.5 times slower than `main`'s Glass default, and issue #45 adds its own step. With a temporary 45-minute limit, the job measured 16 min 45 s (run 41243894083): the issue #27 step took 5 min instead of 1 min 53 s. On a busy runner (run 41246513747, every step 1.3 to 1.5 times slower) WebKit took 23 min 51 s, and Chromium hit its 15 minutes. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)\n\nLinks Notation is the portable, human-readable syntax for nested links\nnetworks. Formal AI uses the parser crate when reading `.lino` input and keeps\nthe notation as the durable interchange format for seeds, memory, datasets,\npackages, and reasoning traces. This is why stored knowledge remains\ninspectable independently of the native or browser backend.\n\n### `lino-objects-codec`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)\n\nThis codec parses and formats object-shaped data expressed in Links Notation.\nFormal AI uses it at strict import boundaries and for canonical structured\nserialization, including associative packages and memory/substitution data.\nFor example, `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `rust/src/associative_package.rs` use the\ncodec's indented-format parser before accepting input.\n\n### `meta-language`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)\n\n`meta-language` represents source text and documents as a mutable links\nnetwork. In `rust/src/coding/cst.rs`, Formal AI uses its real grammars to parse\ngenerated programs, inspect the concrete syntax tree (CST), project AST-like\nstructure, verify a full match, and confirm lossless text reconstruction.\n`rust/src/document_formats.rs` uses the same network for supported markup and\ndocument conversions. It is an optional Cargo feature but is enabled by\ndefault.\n\n### `link-calculator`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator)\n\nThis component evaluates calculator-shaped expressions and returns the value,\nsteps, and a Links Notation trace. `rust/src/calculation.rs` delegates supported\ncalculation input to `link-calculator` first, then uses Formal AI's local\nfallback for syntax or word-problem normalization the component does not\nsupport.\n\n### `lino-arguments`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n\n`lino-arguments` is the configuration boundary for the executable. `rust/src/main.rs`\ninitializes it before parsing commands, allowing Formal AI's CLI options to be\npopulated consistently from command-line arguments, environment variables, and\n`.lenv` files. It configures the system; it does not perform reasoning.\n\n### `lino-i18n`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)\n\nThis JavaScript package parses Links Notation translation catalogs and resolves\nlocalized messages. It is declared in `package.json`, bundled for browser use,\nand loaded by `js/i18n.js`. Its boundary is web internationalization; it is\nnot part of the Rust solver.\n\n### `command-stream`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` declares the native command execution dependency. In\n`rust/src/orchestration/runner.rs`, `execute` passes an exact program/argument\nvector, working directory and environment to `StreamingRunner::from_argv`.\n`collect_command_stream` consumes stdout, stderr and exit events, with a bounded\nexecution timeout and process cancellation. This is the execution boundary for\nexternal agent commands; it does not itself provide reasoning or link storage.\nThe manifest declaration is unconditional, while this orchestration is a native\nhost facility, not a browser subprocess API.\n\n### `web-capture`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` selects `default-features = false` and the `search` feature under\n`cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`. The native acquisition path in\n`rust/src/web_search_core.rs` calls `web_capture::search::build_search_url` and\n`parse_search_results`, recording blocked, empty and unavailable observations.\nThis supplies search acquisition/parsing rather than a knowledge-store backend;\nfailed acquisition is evidence of a failure, not an answer.\n\nThe browser component in `js/web-search-component-entry.js` uses an HTTP capture\nadapter: it first requests `/fetch?url=…` from the configured capture base\n(default `http://localhost:3000`) with a deadline. A transport failure can fall\nback to a direct CORS fetch. The adapter preserves the target status and bytes,\nincluding target HTTP errors; a target error must not be misrepresented as a\nsuccessful discovery. This browser HTTP boundary is distinct from compiling the\nnative Cargo dependency into WASM.\n\n### `web-search`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search)\n\nThere are two direct package integrations, with versions governed by their\nrespective manifests:\n\n- Native: `rust/Cargo.toml` declares `web-search` without default features and with\n  `merge`, under `cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`.\n  `rust/src/web_search_core.rs` converts provider rankings to `SearchResult`,\n  configures `MergeOptions` with the shared reciprocal-rank-fusion constant and\n  calls `web_search::merger::merge_results`.\n- JavaScript: `package.json` declares `@link-assistant/web-search`.\n  `js/web-search-component-entry.js` imports and actually calls\n  `getDefaultProviderIds` and `mergeResults`. Its merge uses reciprocal rank\n  fusion and duplicate removal; its HTTP adapter supplies captured pages.\n\nSearch discovers candidate evidence; capture obtains it; ranking merges the\ncandidates. Formal AI still owns the reasoning and verification needed to turn\nthose observations into supported statements. Neither package substitutes for\nthat reasoning, proves the content true, or provides a link-store dependency.\n\n## Architecture and protocol components\n\nThese repositories explain protocol lineage, compatibility, or design context.\nUnless a component is explicitly described as a direct dependency above, it is\nnot linked into the Formal AI runtime.\n\n### Browser storage: `doublets-web`\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)\n\n`doublets-web` is the browser-side Links Platform store and a compatibility\ntarget, not a bundled JavaScript dependency. `js/memory.js` uses an\nIndexedDB implementation with the same event-to-doublets projection and reports\nthe `doublets-web` backend when a compatible global runtime is available. This\nkeeps browser data portable without claiming that the upstream package is\nalways loaded.\n\n### Query dialect supplied by `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nBesides the native storage APIs used directly above, `link-cli` defines the\nlink query and substitution command conventions. Formal AI adapts those\nconventions in `rust/src/links_query.rs` and `rust/src/links_substitution_query/`; it\nlinks the Rust library in-process and does not launch an external CLI binary.\n\n### Reasoning model: `relative-meta-logic`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic)\n\nRelative Meta Logic models claims relative to contexts instead of forcing one\nglobal truth value. Formal AI has an in-repository implementation in\n`rust/src/relative_meta_logic.rs`, integrated with `rust/src/world_model.rs` for\ncontext-relative facts, contradictions, and queries. The upstream repository\nis the architectural reference, not a linked crate.\n\n### Conceptual model: `meta-theory`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-theory](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory)\n\nMeta Theory is a conceptual foundation for describing languages and theories as\ndata. It informs Formal AI's data-first approach to rules, syntax, and\nreasoning, but there is no `meta-theory` runtime dependency in the manifests.\n\n### Transformation model: `transformer`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer)\n\nTransformer is a related model for graph transformations. Formal AI's current\nsubstitution engine is an in-repository implementation in\n`rust/src/substitution.rs`, where `.lino` rules match and rewrite link patterns on\nCRUD events. The repository is useful for comparison and vocabulary, but its\ncode is not linked into the Formal AI runtime.\n\n## Development and orchestration components\n\nThese tools exercise or coordinate the system during development. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)\n\nLinks Notation is the portable, human-readable syntax for nested links\nnetworks. Formal AI uses the parser crate when reading `.lino` input and keeps\nthe notation as the durable interchange format for seeds, memory, datasets,\npackages, and reasoning traces. This is why stored knowledge remains\ninspectable independently of the native or browser backend.\n\n### `lino-objects-codec`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)\n\nThis codec parses and formats object-shaped data expressed in Links Notation.\nFormal AI uses it at strict import boundaries and for canonical structured\nserialization, including associative packages and memory/substitution data.\nFor example, `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `rust/src/associative_package.rs` use the\ncodec's indented-format parser before accepting input.\n\n### `meta-language`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)\n\n`meta-language` represents source text and documents as a mutable links\nnetwork. In `rust/src/coding/cst.rs`, Formal AI uses its real grammars to parse\ngenerated programs, inspect the concrete syntax tree (CST), project AST-like\nstructure, verify a full match, and confirm lossless text reconstruction.\n`rust/src/document_formats.rs` uses the same network for supported markup and\ndocument conversions. It is an optional Cargo feature but is enabled by\ndefault.\n\n### `link-calculator`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator)\n\nThis component evaluates calculator-shaped expressions and returns the value,\nsteps, and a Links Notation trace. `rust/src/calculation.rs` delegates supported\ncalculation input to `link-calculator` first, then uses Formal AI's local\nfallback for syntax or word-problem normalization the component does not\nsupport.\n\n### `lino-arguments`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n\n`lino-arguments` is the configuration boundary for the executable. `rust/src/main.rs`\ninitializes it before parsing commands, allowing Formal AI's CLI options to be\npopulated consistently from command-line arguments, environment variables, and\n`.lenv` files. It configures the system; it does not perform reasoning.\n\n### `lino-i18n`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)\n\nThis JavaScript package parses Links Notation translation catalogs and resolves\nlocalized messages. It is declared in `package.json`, bundled for browser use,\nand loaded by `js/i18n.js`. Its boundary is web internationalization; it is\nnot part of the Rust solver.\n\n### `command-stream`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` declares the native command execution dependency. In\n`rust/src/orchestration/runner.rs`, `execute` passes an exact program/argument\nvector, working directory and environment to `StreamingRunner::from_argv`.\n`collect_command_stream` consumes stdout, stderr and exit events, with a bounded\nexecution timeout and process cancellation. This is the execution boundary for\nexternal agent commands; it does not itself provide reasoning or link storage.\nThe manifest declaration is unconditional, while this orchestration is a native\nhost facility, not a browser subprocess API.\n\n### `web-capture`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` selects `default-features = false` and the `search` feature under\n`cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`. The native acquisition path in\n`rust/src/web_search_core.rs` calls `web_capture::search::build_search_url` and\n`parse_search_results`, recording blocked, empty and unavailable observations.\nThis supplies search acquisition/parsing rather than a knowledge-store backend;\nfailed acquisition is evidence of a failure, not an answer.\n\nThe browser component in `js/web-search-component-entry.js` uses an HTTP capture\nadapter: it first requests `/fetch?url=…` from the configured capture base\n(default `http://localhost:3000`) with a deadline. A transport failure can fall\nback to a direct CORS fetch. The adapter preserves the target status and bytes,\nincluding target HTTP errors; a target error must not be misrepresented as a\nsuccessful discovery. This browser HTTP boundary is distinct from compiling the\nnative Cargo dependency into WASM.\n\n### `web-search`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search)\n\nThere are two direct package integrations, with versions governed by their\nrespective manifests:\n\n- Native: `rust/Cargo.toml` declares `web-search` without default features and with\n  `merge`, under `cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`.\n  `rust/src/web_search_core.rs` converts provider rankings to `SearchResult`,\n  configures `MergeOptions` with the shared reciprocal-rank-fusion constant and\n  calls `web_search::merger::merge_results`.\n- JavaScript: `package.json` declares `@link-assistant/web-search`.\n  `js/web-search-component-entry.js` imports and actually calls\n  `getDefaultProviderIds` and `mergeResults`. Its merge uses reciprocal rank\n  fusion and duplicate removal; its HTTP adapter supplies captured pages.\n\nSearch discovers candidate evidence; capture obtains it; ranking merges the\ncandidates. Formal AI still owns the reasoning and verification needed to turn\nthose observations into supported statements. Neither package substitutes for\nthat reasoning, proves the content true, or provides a link-store dependency.\n\n## Architecture and protocol components\n\nThese repositories explain protocol lineage, compatibility, or design context.\nUnless a component is explicitly described as a direct dependency above, it is\nnot linked into the Formal AI runtime.\n\n### Browser storage: `doublets-web`\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-web](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web)\n\n`doublets-web` is the browser-side Links Platform store and a compatibility\ntarget, not a bundled JavaScript dependency. `js/memory.js` uses an\nIndexedDB implementation with the same event-to-doublets projection and reports\nthe `doublets-web` backend when a compatible global runtime is available. This\nkeeps browser data portable without claiming that the upstream package is\nalways loaded.\n\n### Query dialect supplied by `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nBesides the native storage APIs used directly above, `link-cli` defines the\nlink query and substitution command conventions. Formal AI adapts those\nconventions in `rust/src/links_query.rs` and `rust/src/links_substitution_query/`; it\nlinks the Rust library in-process and does not launch an external CLI binary.\n\n### Reasoning model: `relative-meta-logic`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic)\n\nRelative Meta Logic models claims relative to contexts instead of forcing one\nglobal truth value. Formal AI has an in-repository implementation in\n`rust/src/relative_meta_logic.rs`, integrated with `rust/src/world_model.rs` for\ncontext-relative facts, contradictions, and queries. The upstream repository\nis the architectural reference, not a linked crate.\n\n### Conceptual model: `meta-theory`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-theory](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory)\n\nMeta Theory is a conceptual foundation for describing languages and theories as\ndata. It informs Formal AI's data-first approach to rules, syntax, and\nreasoning, but there is no `meta-theory` runtime dependency in the manifests.\n\n### Transformation model: `transformer`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/transformer](https://github.com/link-foundation/transformer)\n\nTransformer is a related model for graph transformations. Formal AI's current\nsubstitution engine is an in-repository implementation in\n`rust/src/substitution.rs`, where `.lino` rules match and rewrite link patterns on\nCRUD events. The repository is useful for comparison and vocabulary, but its\ncode is not linked into the Formal AI runtime.\n\n## Development and orchestration components\n\nThese tools exercise or coordinate the system during development. They are not",

Layers of sharp\n * sprites pass `{ resolution: false }` and only lower their frames per second.\n */\nexport function governor({ resolution = true } = {}) {\n  const state = { scale: 1, fps: 1 };\n  let seen = 0;\n  let slow = 0;\n  let spent = 0;\n  // The first window is the start of the page (scripts, fonts, layout): not judged.\n  let warm = false;\n  const watch = (gap) => {\n    // A long gap is a hidden tab or a pause of the debugger, not a slow frame.\n    if (!(gap > 0) || gap > 1000) return false;\n    seen++;\n    spent += gap;\n    if (gap > SLOW_GAP) slow++;\n    if (seen < WINDOW && spent < WINDOW_MS) return false;\n    const struggling = slow > seen / 2;\n    seen = 0;\n    slow = 0;\n    spent = 0;\n    if (!warm) {\n      warm = true;\n      return false;\n    }\n    if (!struggling) return false;\n    if (resolution && state.scale > MIN_SCALE)\n      state.scale = Math.max(MIN_SCALE, Number((state.scale * 0.7).toFixed(3)));\n    else if (state.fps > MIN_FPS) state.fps = Math.max(MIN_FPS, state.fps / 2);\n    else return false;\n    return true;\n  };\n  watch.state = state;\n  return watch;\n}\n// Background canvases take their size from CSS (issue #13). Safari may run\n// `<script type=\"module\">` before the stylesheet is applied (WebKit bug 261655,\n// https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=261655), so the first measurement can\n// be the default canvas size of 300×150; when the stylesheet arrives the canvas\n// grows without a window resize event, and its small bitmap would be stretched\n// over the whole screen. A ResizeObserver on the canvas itself catches that;\n// the window resize event is still needed for changes of devicePixelRatio\n// (browser zoom, moving the window to another screen).\n\n/** Device pixels per CSS pixel, at most 2: sharper is not visible on a background. */\nexport const pixelRatio = () => Math.min((typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.devicePixelRatio) || 1, 2);\n\n/** Calls `onResize()` whenever `element` or the window changes size; returns a function that stops watching. */\nexport function watchSize(element, onResize) {\n  const observer = typeof ResizeObserver === 'function' ? new ResizeObserver(() => onResize()) : null;\n  observer?.observe(element);\n  window.addEventListener('resize', onResize);\n  return () => {\n    observer?.disconnect();\n    window.removeEventListener('resize', onResize);\n  };\n}",

[2026-11-01T16:03:45.996Z] [INFO]         "content": "# Associative technology stack\n\nFormal AI stores inspectable knowledge as a links network with Links Notation as its portable text representation.\n\nThis guide names the upstream associative components, explains what each one\nprovides, and states exactly where Formal AI uses it.\n\n“Associative” here means that knowledge is represented as addressable links\nbetween other links or values. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)\n\nLinks Notation is the portable, human-readable syntax for nested links\nnetworks. Formal AI uses the parser crate when reading `.lino` input and keeps\nthe notation as the durable interchange format for seeds, memory, datasets,\npackages, and reasoning traces. This is why stored knowledge remains\ninspectable independently of the native or browser backend.\n\n### `lino-objects-codec`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)\n\nThis codec parses and formats object-shaped data expressed in Links Notation.\nFormal AI uses it at strict import boundaries and for canonical structured\nserialization, including associative packages and memory/substitution data.\nFor example, `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `rust/src/associative_package.rs` use the\ncodec's indented-format parser before accepting input.\n\n### `meta-language`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)\n\n`meta-language` represents source text and documents as a mutable links\nnetwork. In `rust/src/coding/cst.rs`, Formal AI uses its real grammars to parse\ngenerated programs, inspect the concrete syntax tree (CST), project AST-like\nstructure, verify a full match, and confirm lossless text reconstruction.\n`rust/src/document_formats.rs` uses the same network for supported markup and\ndocument conversions. It is an optional Cargo feature but is enabled by\ndefault.\n\n### `link-calculator`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator)\n\nThis component evaluates calculator-shaped expressions and returns the value,\nsteps, and a Links Notation trace. `rust/src/calculation.rs` delegates supported\ncalculation input to `link-calculator` first, then uses Formal AI's local\nfallback for syntax or word-problem normalization the component does not\nsupport.\n\n### `lino-arguments`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n\n`lino-arguments` is the configuration boundary for the executable. `rust/src/main.rs`\ninitializes it before parsing commands, allowing Formal AI's CLI options to be\npopulated consistently from command-line arguments, environment variables, and\n`.lenv` files. It configures the system; it does not perform reasoning.\n\n### `lino-i18n`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)\n\nThis JavaScript package parses Links Notation translation catalogs and resolves\nlocalized messages. It is declared in `package.json`, bundled for browser use,\nand loaded by `js/i18n.js`. Its boundary is web internationalization; it is\nnot part of the Rust solver.\n\n### `command-stream`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/command-stream](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` declares the native command execution dependency. In\n`rust/src/orchestration/runner.rs`, `execute` passes an exact program/argument\nvector, working directory and environment to `StreamingRunner::from_argv`.\n`collect_command_stream` consumes stdout, stderr and exit events, with a bounded\nexecution timeout and process cancellation. This is the execution boundary for\nexternal agent commands; it does not itself provide reasoning or link storage.\nThe manifest declaration is unconditional, while this orchestration is a native\nhost facility, not a browser subprocess API.\n\n### `web-capture`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-capture](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture)\n\n`rust/Cargo.toml` selects `default-features = false` and the `search` feature under\n`cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`. The native acquisition path in\n`rust/src/web_search_core.rs` calls `web_capture::search::build_search_url` and\n`parse_search_results`, recording blocked, empty and unavailable observations.\nThis supplies search acquisition/parsing rather than a knowledge-store backend;\nfailed acquisition is evidence of a failure, not an answer.\n\nThe browser component in `js/web-search-component-entry.js` uses an HTTP capture\nadapter: it first requests `/fetch?url=…` from the configured capture base\n(default `http://localhost:3000`) with a deadline. A transport failure can fall\nback to a direct CORS fetch. The adapter preserves the target status and bytes,\nincluding target HTTP errors; a target error must not be misrepresented as a\nsuccessful discovery. This browser HTTP boundary is distinct from compiling the\nnative Cargo dependency into WASM.\n\n### `web-search`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/web-search](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-search)\n\nThere are two direct package integrations, with versions governed by their\nrespective manifests:\n\n- Native: `rust/Cargo.toml` declares `web-search` without default features and with\n  `merge`, under `cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))`.\n  `rust/src/web_search_core.rs` converts provider rankings to `SearchResult`,\n  configures `MergeOptions` with the shared reciprocal-rank-fusion constant and\n  calls `web_search::merger::merge_results`.\n- JavaScript: `package.json` declares `@link-assistant/web-search`.\n  `js/web-search-component-entry.js` imports and actually calls\n  `getDefaultProviderIds` and `mergeResults`. Its merge uses reciprocal rank\n  fusion and duplicate removal; its HTTP adapter supplies captured pages.\n\nSearch discovers candidate evidence; capture obtains it; ranking merges the\ncandidates. Formal AI still owns the reasoning and verification needed to turn\nthose observations into supported statements. Neither package substitutes for\nthat reasoning, proves the content true, or provides a link-store dependency.\n\n## Architecture and protocol components\n\nThese repositories explain protocol lineage, compatibility, or design context.\nUnless a component is explicitly described as a direct dependency above, it is\nnot linked into the Formal AI runtime.\n\n### Browser storage: `doublets-web`",

The default documented path is readable recursive indented Links Notation for repository data, with a typed codec available when exact JavaScript type preservation or object identity is required. This library provides:\n\n- Readable recursive indented Links Notation for JSON-style objects\n- Typed serialization/deserialization for JavaScript object graphs with circular reference support\n- Compact JSON to Links Notation conversion utilities\n- Fuzzy matching utilities for string comparison\n\nThese tools enable easy implementation of higher-level features like:\n\n- [LinksNotationManager](https://github.com/konard/follow/blob/main/lino.lib.mjs) - Intermediate application data storage\n- [Q&A Database](https://github.com/konard/hh-job-application-automation/blob/main/src/qa-database.mjs) - Questions and answers database\n\n## Features\n\n- **Readable Indented Format**: Write nested objects and arrays as reviewable recursive Links Notation definitions with `formatIndented({ id, obj })`\n- **Dynamic Parsing**: Parse readable indented data back with `parseIndented({ text })`; quoted references stay strings and unquoted numbers, booleans, and `null` become dynamic values\n- **Typed Object Codec**: Encode JavaScript object graphs to Links Notation with type markers when exact type preservation is required\n- **Typed Support**: Handle all common JavaScript types:\n  - Basic types: `null`, `undefined`, `boolean`, `number`, `string`\n  - Collections: `Array`, `Object`\n  - Special number values: `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity`\n- **Readable by Default**: `encode({ obj })` writes plain, indented text that can be read and reviewed\n- **One Record per Line**: `encodeLine({ obj })` writes the same document on one line and `decodeLine({ notation })` reads it back exactly, so an append-only log stays greppable, tailable and countable by `wc -l`\n- **Object Identity**: Shared references and circular references are preserved by the compact format (`encodeCompact`) via object ids\n- **Full Unicode**: Strings are always written as text — a newline stays a newline and a tab stays a tab, so every word stays greppable; only the characters a form cannot carry are percent-escaped, in a value marked individually as `(escaped \"…\")`\n- **Opt-in Tracing**: Set `LINO_CODEC_DEBUG=1` to trace encoding and decoding, the same way in every language\n- **Compact JSON/Lino Conversion**: Convert between JSON and compact Links Notation with `jsonToLino({ json })` and `linoToJson({ lino })`\n- **Reference Escaping**: Properly escape strings for Links Notation format with `escapeReference({ value })`\n- **Fuzzy Matching**: Find similar strings with Levenshtein distance and keyword similarity\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\nnpm install lino-objects-codec\n```\n\nOr with other package managers:\n\n```bash\n# Bun\nbun add lino-objects-codec\n\n# Yarn\nyarn add lino-objects-codec\n\n# pnpm\npnpm add lino-objects-codec\n```\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```javascript\nimport { formatIndented, parseIndented } from 'lino-objects-codec';\n\nconst data = {\n  title: 'Indian Law',\n  defaultLanguage: 'en',\n  maxLines: 1500,\n  nested: { ok: true },\n  items: ['a', 1],\n};\n\nconst lino = formatIndented({ id: 'obj_root', obj: data });\nconsole.log(lino);\n// Output:\n// obj_root:\n//   title 'Indian Law'\n//   defaultLanguage en\n//   maxLines 1500\n//   nested obj_root_nested\n//   items obj_root_items\n//\n// obj_root_nested:\n//   ok true\n//\n// obj_root_items:\n//   a\n//   1\n\nconst parsed = parseIndented({ text: lino });\nconsole.log(parsed.obj.items[1] === 1);\n// Output: true\n```\n\n`encode({ obj })` writes the readable format. Use `encodeCompact({ obj })` when you\nneed exact JavaScript type preservation, circular references, or shared object\nidentity -- the compact format names shared nodes with `obj_N` ids, which the\nreadable tree has nowhere to put:\n\n```javascript\nimport { encodeCompact, decode } from 'lino-objects-codec';\n\nconst obj = { name: 'root' };\nobj.self = obj;\n\nconst encoded = encodeCompact({ obj });\nconst decoded = decode({ notation: encoded });\n\nconsole.log(decoded.self === decoded);\n// Output: true\n```\n\n## Output Formats\n\n| Function                        | Output                                              |\n| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |\n| `encode({ obj })`               | Readable, indented Links Notation (the default)     |\n| `encode({ obj, indent: '\\t' })` | Same, with a custom indentation string              |\n| `encodeLine({ obj })`           | The same document on one line, for append-only logs |\n| `encodeCompact({ obj })`        | The previous single-line, base64 form               |\n| `encodeObfuscated({ obj })`     | Alias of `encodeCompact`                            |\n\n`decode({ notation })` accepts every one of them, so files written by older\nversions keep working and are rewritten in the readable form the next time they\nare saved.\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Public value formatting\n\n`formatValueSingleLine(text)` returns a readable string value with no CR/LF.\n`formatValueVerbatim(text)` retains real newlines and tabs. Both use the same\nquoting and escaping as `encode`, and `decode` recovers the original text:\n\n```javascript\nimport { decode, formatValueSingleLine } from 'lino-objects-codec';\n\nconst text = 'quoted \"value\"\\nnext line';\nconst value = formatValueSingleLine(text);\nconsole.assert(!value.includes('\\n'));\nconsole.assert(decode(value) === text);\n```\n\n### Readable Indented Data\n\n```javascript\nimport { formatIndented, parseIndented } from 'lino-objects-codec';\n\nconst data = {\n  catalog: {\n    title: 'Indian Law',\n    languages: ['en', 'hi'],\n  },\nShell cwd was reset to /tmp/gh-issue-solver-1793547642620",

only the characters a form cannot carry are percent-escaped, in a value marked individually as `(escaped \"…\")`\n- **Opt-in Tracing**: Set `LINO_CODEC_DEBUG=1` to trace encoding and decoding, the same way in every language\n- **Compact JSON/Lino Conversion**: Convert between JSON and compact Links Notation with `jsonToLino({ json })` and `linoToJson({ lino })`\n- **Reference Escaping**: Properly escape strings for Links Notation format with `escapeReference({ value })`\n- **Fuzzy Matching**: Find similar strings with Levenshtein distance and keyword similarity\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\nnpm install lino-objects-codec\n```\n\nOr with other package managers:\n\n```bash\n# Bun\nbun add lino-objects-codec\n\n# Yarn\nyarn add lino-objects-codec\n\n# pnpm\npnpm add lino-objects-codec\n```\n\n## Quick Start\n\n```javascript\nimport { formatIndented, parseIndented } from 'lino-objects-codec';\n\nconst data = {\n  title: 'Indian Law',\n  defaultLanguage: 'en',\n  maxLines: 1500,\n  nested: { ok: true },\n  items: ['a', 1],\n};\n\nconst lino = formatIndented({ id: 'obj_root', obj: data });\nconsole.log(lino);\n// Output:\n// obj_root:\n//   title 'Indian Law'\n//   defaultLanguage en\n//   maxLines 1500\n//   nested obj_root_nested\n//   items obj_root_items\n//\n// obj_root_nested:\n//   ok true\n//\n// obj_root_items:\n//   a\n//   1\n\nconst parsed = parseIndented({ text: lino });\nconsole.log(parsed.obj.items[1] === 1);\n// Output: true\n```\n\n`encode({ obj })` writes the readable format. Both use the same\nquoting and escaping as `encode`, and `decode` recovers the original text:\n\n```javascript\nimport { decode, formatValueSingleLine } from 'lino-objects-codec';\n\nconst text = 'quoted \"value\"\\nnext line';\nconst value = formatValueSingleLine(text);\nconsole.assert(!value.includes('\\n'));\nconsole.assert(decode(value) === text);\n```\n\n### Readable Indented Data\n\n```javascript\nimport { formatIndented, parseIndented } from 'lino-objects-codec';\n\nconst data = {\n  catalog: {\n    title: 'Indian Law',\n    languages: ['en', 'hi'],\n  },",

A stylesheet cannot select an element by its own size, so\n// this script measures the framed elements of every level with limits and marks\n// those outside them with `data-fx-fit=\"<level>\"`; src/skins.frames.fit.css then\n// draws their corners times the fit scale of the level.\n//\n// It costs nothing until a level has limits: then one ResizeObserver measures\n// the elements of those levels (the browser reports a size only when it\n// changes, after layout, so reading it forces no layout), and one\n// MutationObserver finds the elements a new page adds. An attribute is written\n// only when it changes.\nimport { BLOCKS, CONTROL_TYPES, INNER, PANELS } from './skins.frames.js';\nimport { FIT_ATTR, FIT_LEVELS } from './skins.frames.fit.js';\nimport { drawsFrame, FIT_LIMITS, hasFitLimits, levelKey } from './settings/schema.skins.js';\n\n/** Turn on to log every element that changes its mark (`localStorage.debugFrameFit = '1'`). */\nconst debug = () => {\n  try {\n    return globalThis.localStorage?.getItem('debugFrameFit') === '1';\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n};\n\nconst CONTROL_SELECTORS = Object.entries(CONTROL_TYPES).map(([type, selectors]) => [type, selectors.join(', ')]);\nconst BLOCK_SELECTOR = `${INNER}, ${BLOCKS.join(', ')}`;\nconst PANEL_SELECTOR = PANELS.join(', ');\n\n/** The level of the frame an element draws: a type of control, an inner block or an outer panel. */\nexport function levelOf(element) {\n  for (const [type, selector] of CONTROL_SELECTORS) if (element.matches(selector)) return type;\n  if (element.matches(BLOCK_SELECTOR)) return 'block';\n  if (element.matches(PANEL_SELECTOR)) return 'panel';\n  return null;\n}\n\n/**\n * The limits of every level that has some and draws the frame,\n * `{ button: [minWidth, maxWidth, minHeight, maxHeight] }` (0 is no limit), or\n * null when no element needs measuring (another skin or frame, or no limits).\n */\nexport function limitsOf(settings) {\n  if (settings['skin.name'] !== 'futuristic' || settings['future.frame'] !== 'custom') return null;\n  const levels = FIT_LEVELS.filter((level) => drawsFrame(level, settings) && hasFitLimits(level, settings));\n  if (!levels.length) return null;\n  return Object.fromEntries(\n    levels.map((level) => [level, FIT_LIMITS.map(([name]) => settings[levelKey(level, name)])]),\n  );\n}\n\n/** Whether a size is outside the limits [minWidth, maxWidth, minHeight, maxHeight]; [...(node.matches(selector) ? [node] : []), ...node.querySelectorAll(selector)] : [];\n\n  const stop = () => {\n    sizes?.disconnect();\n    mutations?.disconnect();\n    sizes = mutations = null;\n    observed.clear();\n    root.querySelectorAll(`[${FIT_ATTR}]`).forEach((element) => element.removeAttribute(FIT_ATTR));\n  };\n\n  const start = () => {\n    const selector = selectorOf(limits);\n    sizes = new ResizeObserver((entries) => entries.forEach((entry) => mark(entry.target, ...sizeOf(entry))));\n    mutations = new MutationObserver((records) =>\n      records.forEach((record) => {\n        record.addedNodes.forEach((node) => within(node, selector).forEach(observe));\n        record.removedNodes.forEach((node) => {\n          if (node.nodeType !== 1) return;\n          // Forget the elements that left the page, or the observer keeps them.\n          observed.forEach((element) => {\n            if (element === node || node.contains(element)) forget(element);\n          });\n        });\n      }),\n    );\n    mutations.observe(root, { childList: true, subtree: true });\n    // The first report of every observed element marks it.\n    within(root, selector).forEach(observe);\n  };\n\n  const sync = () => {\n    const next = limitsOf(getSettings());\n    const nextKey = JSON.stringify(next);\n    if (nextKey === key) return;\n    key = nextKey;\n    stop();\n    limits = next;\n    if (limits) start();\n  };\n\n  sync();\n  const unsubscribe = subscribe(sync);\n  return () => {\n    unsubscribe();\n    stop();\n  };\n}\n"

It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)\n\nLinks Notation is the portable, human-readable syntax for nested links\nnetworks. Formal AI uses the parser crate when reading `.lino` input and keeps\nthe notation as the durable interchange format for seeds, memory, datasets,\npackages, and reasoning traces. This is why stored knowledge remains\ninspectable independently of the native or browser backend.\n\n### `lino-objects-codec`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-objects-codec](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec)\n\nThis codec parses and formats object-shaped data expressed in Links Notation.\nFormal AI uses it at strict import boundaries and for canonical structured\nserialization, including associative packages and memory/substitution data.\nFor example, `rust/src/link_store.rs` and `rust/src/associative_package.rs` use the\ncodec's indented-format parser before accepting input.\n\n### `meta-language`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/meta-language](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language)\n\n`meta-language` represents source text and documents as a mutable links\nnetwork. In `rust/src/coding/cst.rs`, Formal AI uses its real grammars to parse\ngenerated programs, inspect the concrete syntax tree (CST), project AST-like\nstructure, verify a full match, and confirm lossless text reconstruction.\n`rust/src/document_formats.rs` uses the same network for supported markup and\ndocument conversions. It is an optional Cargo feature but is enabled by\ndefault.\n\n### `link-calculator`\n\nRepository: [link-assistant/calculator](https://github.com/link-assistant/calculator)\n\nThis component evaluates calculator-shaped expressions and returns the value,\nsteps, and a Links Notation trace. `rust/src/calculation.rs` delegates supported\ncalculation input to `link-calculator` first, then uses Formal AI's local\nfallback for syntax or word-problem normalization the component does not\nsupport.\n\n### `lino-arguments`\n\nRepository:\n[link-foundation/lino-arguments](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments)\n\n`lino-arguments` is the configuration boundary for the executable. `rust/src/main.rs`\ninitializes it before parsing commands, allowing Formal AI's CLI options to be\npopulated consistently from command-line arguments, environment variables, and\n`.lenv` files. It configures the system; it does not perform reasoning.\n\n### `lino-i18n`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/lino-i18n](https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-i18n)\n\nThis JavaScript package parses Links Notation translation catalogs and resolves\nlocalized messages. It is declared in `package.json`, bundled for browser use,\nand loaded by `js/i18n.js`. Its boundary is web internationalization; it is\nnot part of the Rust solver.\n\n### `command-stream`",

Every parse calls `trace()` (`format.js` → `trace('format.parseIndented', …)`, `codec.js` → `trace('codec.decode', …)`, `readable.js` → `trace('readable.decode', …)`). `trace()` calls `isDebugEnabled()`, and that reads the environment with no guard:\n\n```js\nexport function isDebugEnabled() {\n  if (overridden !== null) {\n    return overridden;\n  }\n  const raw = process.env[DEBUG_ENV_VAR];\n```\n\nA related problem: `decode` of a legacy `(base64 \"…\")` value (`readable.js` `decodeMarkedValue`) uses `Buffer.from(…, 'base64')`, so it throws `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined` in a browser too. `codec.js` (`encodeCompact` and its decoding) uses `Buffer` the same way.\n\n## Reproduction\n\nThis Node script removes the two Node globals a browser does not have, then loads the codec:\n\n```js\n// repro.mjs — node repro.mjs (lino-objects-codec 0.9.4)\ndelete globalThis.process;\ndelete globalThis.Buffer;\nconst codec = await import('lino-objects-codec');\nconst attempt = (title, run) => {\n  try { console.log('ok  ', title, JSON.stringify(run())); Decode and encode base64 without `Buffer` when it is missing, e.g. with `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` and `atob`/`btoa`:\n\n```js\nconst fromBase64 = (b64) =>\n  typeof Buffer !== 'undefined'\n    ? Buffer.from(b64, 'base64').toString('utf-8')\n    : new TextDecoder().decode(Uint8Array.from(atob(b64), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0)));\n```\n\n3. Add a test that runs the parsers with `process` and `Buffer` removed, like the script above, so the browser path stays covered.\nEOF\ngh issue create --repo link-foundation/lino-objects-codec --title \"parseIndented and decode throw \\\"process is not defined\\\" in a browser (unguarded process.env in debug.js; Buffer in base64 decoding)\" --body-file /tmp/upstream-issue.md"

id as the fit limits reveal more of them (issue #47)\n\n# Associative technology stack\n\nFormal AI stores inspectable knowledge as a links network with Links Notation as its portable text representation.\n\nThis guide names the upstream associative components, explains what each one\nprovides, and states exactly where Formal AI uses it.\n\n“Associative” here means that knowledge is represented as addressable links\nbetween other links or values. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. representation.\n\nThis guide names the upstream associative components, explains what each one\nprovides, and states exactly where Formal AI uses it.\n\n“Associative” here means that knowledge is represented as addressable links\nbetween other links or values. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. Research: existing libraries and platform features\n\n| Option | What it offers | Why it is or is not used |\n# Associative technology stack\n\nFormal AI stores inspectable knowledge as a links network with Links Notation as its portable text representation.\n\nThis guide names the upstream associative components, explains what each one\nprovides, and states exactly where Formal AI uses it.\n\n“Associative” here means that knowledge is represented as addressable links\nbetween other links or values. It does not mean that every repository in the\nsame ecosystem is compiled into Formal AI. The sections below distinguish:\n\n- a **direct dependency** declared in `Cargo.toml` or `package.json`;\n- a protocol, compatibility target, or in-repository implementation informed\n  by another project; and\n- a development-time tool that operates Formal AI without becoming part of the\n  shipped runtime.\n\n## How data moves through the stack\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n    Clients[\"CLI / HTTP / browser\"] --> Config[\"lino-arguments\"]\n    Config --> Syntax[\"Links Notation + object codec\"]\n    Syntax --> Store[\"link-cli transactional store<br/>or browser IndexedDB\"]\n    Store --> Reason[\"Formal AI reasoning,<br/>query and substitution\"]\n    Syntax --> Meta[\"meta-language CST / AST\"]\n    Reason --> Calc[\"link-calculator\"]\n    Reason --> Output[\"Links Notation / API / localized web UI\"]\n    Agent[\"Agent CLI / Hive Mind<br/>(development-time)\"] -.-> Clients\n```\n\n1. `lino-arguments` turns command-line, environment, and `.lenv` settings into\n   Formal AI configuration.\n2. `links-notation` and `lino-objects-codec` parse human-readable `.lino`\n   documents and serialize portable memories, datasets, traces, and packages.\n3. A native default build mirrors those records through the `link-cli` library,\n   whose transactional layer wraps a file-mapped `doublets-rs` store. Browser\n   builds keep the same reducible link shape in IndexedDB and advertise\n   `doublets-web` only when that runtime is present.\n4. Formal AI's in-repository reasoning, query, and substitution engines operate\n   on the links. `meta-language` supplies CST and AST networks for program and\n   document structure, while `link-calculator` handles supported calculations.\n5. Results return through the CLI or API, can be serialized back to Links\n   Notation, and are localized in the web UI through `lino-i18n`.\n\n## Direct runtime components\n\nThese components are current direct dependencies. The manifest and source-path\nreferences are the source of truth for how each is integrated.\n\n### `link-cli`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/link-cli](https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli)\n\nFormal AI's default `doublets-native` Cargo feature selects `link-cli` as its\nnative link-store library. `rust/src/link_store.rs` uses link-cli's file-mapped\n`DoubletsStorage` and `GenericTransactionsDecorator` directly: server writes\nare committed with an fsynced recovery log, explicit rollback restores both\nthe native graph and its in-memory projection, and an interrupted projection is\nrepaired from the atomic `.lino` source on reopen. This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection. Its\n[`platform-mem`](https://github.com/linksplatform/mem-rs) allocator is likewise\ntransitive storage infrastructure, not a separately integrated semantic or\nreasoning layer.\n\n### `links-notation`\n\nRepository: [link-foundation/links-notation](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation)",

This replaces Formal AI's\nformer local composition of `doublets` and `platform-mem`.\n\n### `doublets-rs` storage inside link-cli\n\nRepository: [linksplatform/doublets-rs](https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs)\n\n`doublets-rs` supplies link-cli's physical doublet network: each link has a\nsource and target and can point to other links. It is now a transitive\nimplementation detail of the link-cli library rather than a separately wired\nFormal AI dependency. `rust/src/link_store.rs` reduces memory events to stable\n`Type → SubType → Value` graphs while Links Notation remains the reviewable\nimport/export projection.
